evidence.claim: Olaf Scholz was elected in December 2021 as the ninth Federal Chancellor of Germany and led the first traffic-light coalition at federal level.
evidence.title: Lebenslauf Olaf Scholz
evidence.excerpt: Olaf Scholz was elected in December 2021 as the ninth Federal Chancellor of Germany and led the first traffic-light coalition at federal level.
evidence.source_locator: Biography section near the opening paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official federal biography page with a stable office chronology.
evidence.period_fit: Establishes Scholz's office and inherited baseline for 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Scholz; this is his official office record.
contrary_evidence: None on office status.

evidence.claim: Scholz said that with regard to nuclear sharing Germany would procure a modern replacement for the outdated Tornado jets in good time, and that the F-35 could be used as a carrier aircraft.
evidence.title: Policy statement by Olaf Scholz, Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany and Member of the German Bundestag, 27 February 2022 in Berlin
evidence.excerpt: Scholz said that with regard to nuclear sharing Germany would procure a modern replacement for the outdated Tornado jets in good time, and that the F-35 could be used as a carrier aircraft.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous statement by the Chancellor on the official federal website.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 decision point on Germany's nuclear-sharing posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz statement and policy choice; cabinet-level commitment under his leadership.
contrary_evidence: This preserved rather than reduced Germany's nuclear-sharing role.
Critics later argued it locked Germany into nuclear deterrence for years.

evidence.claim: Scholz said the federal government, Länder, and municipalities would work together to provide Ukrainian refugees with accommodation, medical care, school instruction, and a safe future.
evidence.title: Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz
evidence.excerpt: Scholz said the federal government, Länder, and municipalities would work together to provide Ukrainian refugees with accommodation, medical care, school instruction, and a safe future.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government bulletin with direct speech by the chancellor and exact target-period wording.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 ruler-period evidence on crisis welfare response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Scholz as chancellor; the commitment is government-wide rather than a personal administrative order.
contrary_evidence: This is a pledge and crisis response statement, not proof of long-term outcomes by itself.

evidence.claim: The Bundestag approved the federal government's bill to raise the statutory minimum wage to 12 euros per hour from 1 October 2022, benefiting over six million workers, especially women and people in eastern Germany.
evidence.title: Der Mindestlohn steigt auf 12 Euro
evidence.excerpt: The Bundestag approved the federal government's bill to raise the statutory minimum wage to 12 euros per hour from 1 October 2022, benefiting over six million workers, especially women and people in eastern Germany.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry release on a passed government bill with specific quantified beneficiaries.
evidence.ruler_attribution: A coalition policy implemented through Bundestag legislation under Scholz's government; not a personal administrative act.
contrary_evidence: Inflation and high living costs still eroded real purchasing power in 2022.

evidence.claim: The cabinet approved Wohngeld Plus and the second heating subsidy, described as the largest housing-benefit reform since the program began, supporting roughly 4.5 million people in two million households.
evidence.title: Mehr Geld für die Wohnkosten im Winter
evidence.excerpt: The cabinet approved Wohngeld Plus and the second heating subsidy, described as the largest housing-benefit reform since the program began, supporting roughly 4.5 million people in two million households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry press release with a concrete cabinet decision and beneficiary scale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet policy under Scholz; the measure is institutional and coalition-based rather than personal patronage.
contrary_evidence: The main effect begins in 2023, so this is partly forward-looking rather than immediate 2022 delivery.

evidence.claim: The federal government decided that registered Ukrainian refugees would receive extended basic-security benefits from 1 June 2022, with jobcenter-based access to integration and language courses, labor-market support, childcare support, and health coverage.
evidence.title: Couverture de base pour les réfugiés ukrainiens
evidence.excerpt: The federal government decided that registered Ukrainian refugees would receive extended basic-security benefits from 1 June 2022, with jobcenter-based access to integration and language courses, labor-market support, childcare support, and health coverage.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government archive page with explicit cabinet decision and service details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Federal cabinet action under Scholz; implementation shared with the Länder and local job centers.
contrary_evidence: This is a policy-design document; it does not by itself prove long-run integration outcomes in 2022.

evidence.claim: Scholz said Ukrainian refugees were welcome and that the government would ensure accommodation, medical care, schooling, and a secure future, alongside additional humanitarian funding.
evidence.title: Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz
evidence.excerpt: Scholz said Ukrainian refugees were welcome and that the government would ensure accommodation, medical care, schooling, and a secure future, alongside additional humanitarian funding.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary chancellor speech with direct welfare and refugee-protection commitments.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Scholz as chancellor.
contrary_evidence: This is a commitment speech, not a delivery audit.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the government was expanding income support for vulnerable households, cutting fuel taxes, and providing liquidity support to firms, and the Executive Board commended the authorities' timely and well-designed response to the Ukraine spillovers.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with Germany
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the government was expanding income support for vulnerable households, cutting fuel taxes, and providing liquidity support to firms, and the Executive Board commended the authorities' timely and well-designed response to the Ukraine spillovers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral assessment of the government's 2022 policy response with concrete policy details and evaluative language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: External appraisal of the Scholz government's response; not a personal evaluation of every implementing agency.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also noted that some broad-based relief measures, such as fuel-tax cuts, were fiscally costly and distorted price signals.

evidence.claim: The OECD said the government took bold actions to support households and firms, with three relief packages and a 200 billion euro energy support fund that included social assistance, housing allowances, one-off transfers, and permanent policy changes such as an inflation adjustment of the tax schedule and reform of the housing allowance system.
evidence.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Germany 2023
evidence.excerpt: The OECD said the government took bold actions to support households and firms, with three relief packages and a 200 billion euro energy support fund that included social assistance, housing allowances, one-off transfers, and permanent policy changes such as an inflation adjustment of the tax schedule and reform of the housing allowance system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral economic assessment with detailed package composition and policy critique.
evidence.period_fit: Retroactive evaluation of 2022 policy response and 2023 reform design.
evidence.ruler_attribution: External assessment of the Scholz government's policy choices; the government is credited for the package, not for every outcome effect.
contrary_evidence: The OECD also said the measures were not well targeted at vulnerable households and highly exposed firms.

evidence.claim: Average employment in 2022 reached about 45.6 million people, a record high since German unification, rising by 589,000 from the previous year.
evidence.title: Employment in 2022 at highest level since German unification
evidence.excerpt: Average employment in 2022 reached about 45.6 million people, a record high since German unification, rising by 589,000 from the previous year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official statistics release with clear headline figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Macro outcome under Scholz's year in office, but heavily conditioned by preexisting labor-market strength and immigration.
contrary_evidence: Employment strength does not offset the simultaneous erosion in real wages and persistent poverty risk.

evidence.claim: The government set up the ExpertInnen-Kommission Gas und Wärme on 23 September 2022, then used its proposals to build a 200 billion euro economic shield and gas/heat price brake through mid-2024.
evidence.title: Wirtschaftlicher Abwehrschirm und Gaspreisbremse: mit Entschlossenheit durch die Energiekrise
evidence.excerpt: The government set up the ExpertInnen-Kommission Gas und Wärme on 23 September 2022, then used its proposals to build a 200 billion euro economic shield and gas/heat price brake through mid-2024.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed official ministry report with dates, institutional setup, and implementation architecture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong cabinet-level attribution under Scholz; the report ties the measures to the federal government, though the technical design was commission-led.
contrary_evidence: It shows design and financing, not post-implementation distributional results.
It is a ministry report, so it is stronger on process than independent outcome evaluation.

evidence.claim: The Bürgergeld law was promulgated on 20 December 2022 and entered into force on 1 January 2023, replacing the old basic-security framework for jobseekers.
evidence.title: Bürgergeld-Gesetz
evidence.excerpt: The Bürgergeld law was promulgated on 20 December 2022 and entered into force on 1 January 2023, replacing the old basic-security framework for jobseekers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry legislative tracking with enactment and entry-into-force dates.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and immediately adjacent to the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong cabinet-level attribution: this is the legal enactment path of a central Scholz government social reform, though the page does not isolate the chancellor's personal hand in drafting.
contrary_evidence: It documents enactment, not later service-quality outcomes.
It does not by itself prove the reform reached all intended beneficiaries.

evidence.claim: The Bundestag adopted a new calculation base for unemployment and short-time work benefits for cross-border workers and made easier access to unemployment insurance for short-term workers permanent.
evidence.title: Änderungen im Bereich des Arbeitslosengeldes und Kurzarbeitergeldes
evidence.excerpt: The Bundestag adopted a new calculation base for unemployment and short-time work benefits for cross-border workers and made easier access to unemployment insurance for short-term workers permanent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry statement on a passed legislative change with explicit implementation effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate-to-strong attribution: this is a coalition-backed federal social-policy change under Scholz, though the operational details are ministerial.
contrary_evidence: It is a targeted adjustment, not a broad service-system overhaul.
It shows legal change more than delivery performance.

evidence.claim: The federal family ministry said the Länder and municipalities were responsible for housing and care, while the federal ministry coordinated with them and maintained a central point for evacuated children and youth.
evidence.title: Hilfe und Unterstützung für geflüchtete Menschen aus der Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: The federal family ministry said the Länder and municipalities were responsible for housing and care, while the federal ministry coordinated with them and maintained a central point for evacuated children and youth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry statement with clear operational responsibilities and target groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is a federal response under Scholz's government, but day-to-day delivery sits mainly with Länder and municipalities.
contrary_evidence: The page explicitly says the Länder and municipalities carry primary responsibility.
It documents support architecture more than measured delivery outcomes.

evidence.claim: The ministry opened a hotline and central coordination office to register capacities, distribute evacuated child groups across Länder, and keep groups together with their caregivers.
evidence.title: Koordinierungsstelle zur Aufnahme ukrainischer Waisenkinder nimmt Betrieb auf
evidence.excerpt: The ministry opened a hotline and central coordination office to register capacities, distribute evacuated child groups across Länder, and keep groups together with their caregivers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry operational announcement with concrete procedures and contact details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the program is federal-government-led under Scholz, but the operational mechanism is handled by the ministry and Bundesverwaltungsamt.
contrary_evidence: It does not show how well the system performed after launch.
It is strongest for setup, weaker for long-run durability.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on internal nuclear-safety alternatives and command-and-control review is still thin.
Internal cabinet deliberations and precise alternative options around the Ukraine response are not visible.
Most policing and complaint-handling evidence is Länder-level, so direct Scholz attribution remains limited.
Direct evidence of 2022 Scholz-led democratic strengthening is thinner than evidence of institutional baseline and judicial constraint.
Direct chancellor-level evidence on personnel selection, correction after failure, and anti-capture choices remains limited.
Post-enactment delivery quality and longer-run durability of the reforms are not fully shown in the 2022 package.
Direct primary evidence on assets, gifts, family benefit, hidden conflicts, or formal self-dealing is missing.
The record remains allegation-heavy rather than adjudication-heavy on deception and obstruction.
Direct evidence on Scholz's personnel selection, correction of underperformers, and internal discipline is thinner than evidence on program design and rollout.
